html:
Vacacocha is the name the map gives a small territory in the forests of northern Peru, between the Napo and Curaray rivers in Loreto. Standard sources say little about a people by this name; it may be the name of a local community, since cocha is the Quechua word for a lake.

The area is home to Kichwa-speaking river peoples such as the Napo Kichwa and to smaller groups who lived by fishing, hunting and farming manioc. The rubber boom of the late 1800s brought forced labour and epidemics here, as across the Amazon.
